name: Carkas
overview: Carkas was a male eunuch who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus, identified as one of seven such attendants. His role placed him within the royal court during the time of the Persian king Ahasuerus, as noted in the book of Esther. No further tribal or familial details are provided in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Carkas is a proper name mentioned in Esther 1:10 and is possibly derived from a term meaning 'vulture.' This suggests a name given by human origin rather than directly by God, with no additional titles recorded.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Carkas beyond his role as one of the eunuchs serving King Ahasuerus. There are no known relatives or connections detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Carkas holds significance as part of the inner circle of eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus, indicating a trusted position within the Persian royal household. His inclusion in the narrative highlights the administrative and personal attendants who played roles in the unfolding events of Esther. Though not a central figure, his presence contributes to the setting and context of the king's court.
